home.faq1Q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
home.faq1A: No. All processing happens in your browser. Your files never leave your device and are not sent to our servers or any third party. This applies to every FileFlip tool: images, PDFs, videos, and archives are handled locally.
home.faq2Q: What is the maximum file size?
home.faq2A: Limits depend on your device and browser memory. In practice, files of a few hundred megabytes can often be processed; very large files (e.g. over 1 GB) may cause the browser to slow down or run out of memory. We recommend trying smaller batches if you hit limits.
home.faq3Q: Does it work on iPhone and Android?
home.faq3A: Yes. FileFlip runs in the mobile browser (Safari on iPhone, Chrome or others on Android). You open the site, choose a tool, and upload from your gallery or files. No app install is required. The experience is the same as on desktop, adapted to the screen size.
home.faq4A: No. FileFlip needs an internet connection to load the site and its scripts. Once the page is loaded, the actual file processing runs in your browser and does not require a continuous connection for the duration of the conversion. You need to be online to open and use the tools.
home.faq5Q: How do I convert HEIC to JPG?
home.faq5A: Go to the “HEIC to JPG” tool from the homepage. Upload one or more HEIC files (e.g. from your iPhone). The tool converts them in the browser and lets you download each JPG or all at once in a ZIP. No account or upload to a server is needed. Quality remains high for typical use.
home.faq6Q: Is FileFlip safe for confidential files?
home.faq6A: Yes. Because everything runs in your browser, your files are never sent to our servers or stored by us. For maximum privacy, use FileFlip on a device you control and close the tab when you are done. We do not collect, store, or analyse the contents of your files.
home.faq7Q: Do I need to create an account?
home.faq7A: No. You can use every FileFlip tool without signing up or logging in. Open the site, pick a tool, upload your file, and download the result. We do not require an email, password, or any personal data to use the tools. This keeps usage simple and private.
home.faq8A: Yes. FileFlip is free to use, with no hidden fees or premium tiers. The goal is to offer simple, practical tools for everyone. We do not add watermarks to your results or ask for payment. You can use the tools as often as you like at no cost.

compressImage.label: Compress image
compressImage.short: Reduce the size of your photos.
compressImage.metaDescription: Compress JPG, PNG and WebP photos online for free. Reduce image size while keeping quality. No account, everything in the browser.
compressImage.dropzonePrompt: Drag your image here or click to select
compressImage.editorialTitle: Why compress images, and how to choose format and quality
compressImage.editorialBody:
Image compression reduces file size by removing or simplifying image data, so your photos take less space and load faster. Smaller images mean quicker website loading, easier email attachments, and no hassle with size limits on forms or social media.

Choose the format that fits your use: JPG is best for photos and complex images—it keeps file size low with minimal visible loss. PNG keeps every pixel intact and supports transparency, so use it for logos, screenshots, or graphics with sharp edges. WebP often gives the smallest files at similar quality and is supported by all modern browsers; use it when you want the best balance of size and quality for the web.

The quality slider controls how much compression is applied: higher values (e.g. 80–90) keep more detail and produce larger files; lower values (e.g. 50–60) shrink the file more but can introduce visible artefacts. For most photos, 70–80 is a good starting point—check the preview and adjust until the result looks right and the size fits your needs.
compressImage.qualityHint: Lower = smaller file, lower quality. Try 60–80 for a good balance.
compressImage.step3Description: Save the compressed image to your device.
compressImage.resultPlaceholder: Result will appear here after compression.
compressImage.errorUnsupportedFormat: Unsupported format. Use JPG, PNG or WebP.
compressImage.errorSelectFirst: Select an image to compress first.
compressImage.reductionSimilar: Compressed size is similar to original.
compressImage.faq1Q: How do you compress an image online?
compressImage.faq1A: Upload your photo (JPG, PNG or WebP) using the button, choose a quality level with the slider, then click compress. You can compare the original and compressed result side by side before downloading. Everything runs in your browser, so no data is sent to any server.
compressImage.faq2A: Compression always involves a trade-off between file size and quality. You control this with the quality slider: lower values give smaller files but more visible loss. We recommend trying 60–80 for a good balance. The preview lets you check the result before downloading.
compressImage.faq3A: You can upload and compress JPG (JPEG), PNG and WebP images. The compressed output keeps the same format as the original. These formats cover the vast majority of photos and graphics used on the web and in apps.
compressImage.faq4Q: Are files saved on the server?
compressImage.faq4A: No. All processing happens in your browser. Your images are never uploaded to our servers or stored anywhere. You stay in full control of your files from start to finish.
compressImage.faq5Q: Is there a file size limit?
compressImage.faq5A: There is no fixed limit set by the tool. Practical limits depend on your device and browser memory. Very large images (e.g. tens of megabytes) may take longer to process or, on low-memory devices, cause the browser to slow down. For typical photos (a few MB), there are no issues.
compressImage.faq6Q: What is the difference between JPG and PNG in compression?
compressImage.faq6A: JPG uses lossy compression: it discards some detail to achieve much smaller file sizes, which makes it ideal for photos. PNG uses lossless compression: it keeps every pixel intact but produces larger files, and is better for graphics with sharp edges or transparency. For photos on the web, JPG usually gives the best balance of size and quality; use PNG when you need transparency or exact reproduction of logos and UI elements.
compressImage.faq7Q: How do I compress images for WhatsApp?
compressImage.faq7A: WhatsApp automatically compresses photos when you send them, which can reduce quality. To keep control, compress your image first with this tool at a quality you choose (e.g. 75–80), then send the result: the file will be smaller and may be altered less by WhatsApp. Use JPG for photos; avoid sending huge originals so the app does not apply its own heavy compression. The tool runs in the browser, so you can do it quickly from your phone or computer before sharing.
compressImage.faq8Q: Can I compress multiple images at once?
compressImage.faq8A: Yes. You can add several images in one go: use the upload button and select multiple files, or drag and drop a batch. Each image is compressed separately and you can adjust quality per image if needed. When you are done, download each file individually or use the option to download all as a ZIP. Processing runs in your browser, so there is no limit imposed by the tool—only your device memory for very large batches.
compressImage.faq9A: No. Lossy compression (as used for JPG and WebP at lower quality) permanently removes some image data; you cannot restore the exact original from the compressed file. If you might need the full quality later, keep a copy of the original before compressing. PNG compression is lossless, so the image can be decoded back to the same pixels, but the file size reduction is smaller. This tool does not store your files, so always keep your originals on your device if you want to revert.
compressImage.faq10Q: What is the best format for photos on the web?
compressImage.faq10A: For most photos on websites and blogs, JPG is still the best choice: it gives small file sizes and good visual quality at 75–85% quality. WebP often produces even smaller files at similar quality and is supported by all modern browsers; use it when you want faster page loads. PNG is better for images with transparency or sharp graphics. Save photos as JPG or WebP for hero images, galleries, and thumbnails; use PNG for logos and graphics with transparent backgrounds.
compressImage.faq11Q: Why did my file get bigger after compressing?
compressImage.faq11A: That can happen when the original is already highly compressed or in a format that does not shrink much at the quality you chose. For example, a low-quality JPG re-saved at 90% may grow because you are asking for more quality than the source contains. Try a lower quality setting (e.g. 65–75) or use a format like WebP, which often gives smaller files at similar quality. Screenshots and simple graphics can also sometimes increase in size when saved as JPG at high quality.
compressImage.faq12Q: Does compressing an image affect print quality?
compressImage.faq12A: It can. Lossy compression (JPG, WebP) removes detail that cannot be recovered. For screen use, 75–85% quality is usually fine, but for large prints or professional use you may notice softness or artefacts. If you need the image for print, keep the quality high (85–95) or keep an uncompressed original. This tool is best for reducing file size for web, email, or social media; for print, prefer minimal compression or lossless formats when possible.

mergePdf.label: Merge PDF
mergePdf.short: Combine multiple PDFs into one file.
mergePdf.metaDescription: Combine multiple PDF files into one online. Drag and drop to reorder. No account, works in the browser.
mergePdf.editorialTitle: When and why to merge PDFs
mergePdf.editorialBody: Merging PDFs is useful when you have several documents—reports, scans, or forms—that you want in a single file for sharing or printing. The tool keeps the original quality of each PDF and lets you decide the order by dragging the files. Everything runs in your browser, so your documents never leave your device.
mergePdf.step1Hint: Select multiple files or add them in batches.
mergePdf.step2Hint: Drag rows to change order. Then merge.

mergePdf.errorMinTwoAlt: At least two PDFs are required to merge.

mergePdf.faq1Q: How do I merge PDFs online?
mergePdf.faq1A: Click the button to add one or more PDF files from your device. They appear in a list below. Drag the rows to change the order of the documents. When you are happy with the order, click "Merge PDF" to create a single PDF and download it. The process runs entirely in your browser, so your files never leave your device.
mergePdf.faq2A: You reorder whole documents, not individual pages. Drag the file rows up or down to set the order in which each PDF appears in the merged file. The pages of each PDF keep their internal order; the merged PDF is document 1's pages, then document 2's, and so on. If you need to reorder single pages within a PDF, you would need a separate tool that supports page-level editing.
mergePdf.faq3Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
mergePdf.faq3A: No. Merging is done locally in your browser. Your files never leave your device or get stored on our servers. This keeps your documents private and secure. You can merge sensitive or confidential PDFs without any upload.
mergePdf.faq4Q: Is there a limit to how many PDFs I can merge?
mergePdf.faq4A: There is no fixed limit in the tool. Very large numbers of files or very big PDFs may make the browser use a lot of memory and take longer. For typical documents (e.g. a few dozen PDFs of a few MB each), merging works without issues. If you hit performance limits, try merging in smaller batches and then merging the resulting PDFs.
mergePdf.faq5A: No. The tool combines the existing content of your PDFs without re-encoding or re-compressing the pages. Text and images in the merged PDF stay at the same quality as in the originals. The output is a single PDF that behaves like one continuous document.
mergePdf.faq6Q: Can I remove a file from the list before merging?
mergePdf.faq6A: Yes. Each file in the list has a remove or delete option so you can take it out before clicking Merge. Reorder the remaining files as needed, then merge. If you change your mind, add the file again and adjust the order.
mergePdf.faq7Q: What happens to bookmarks and links in the PDFs?
mergePdf.faq7A: Bookmarks and internal links from the original PDFs are preserved in the merged file where the library supports it. Very complex PDFs with nested bookmarks may have simplified structure in the result. External links and hyperlinks generally remain clickable in the merged PDF.
mergePdf.faq8A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser (Safari on iPhone, Chrome or others on Android). You can add PDFs from your device or cloud storage, reorder them, and download the merged file. No app install is required; processing happens in the browser so file size limits depend on your device's memory.
mergePdf.faq9A: Password-protected (encrypted) PDFs must be unlocked first before this tool can read them. Open the PDF with the correct password in another app, save it without password protection, then use that copy here. The merge tool itself does not ask for or handle PDF passwords.
mergePdf.faq10Q: Can I merge scanned PDFs or image-based PDFs?
mergePdf.faq10A: Yes. Scanned PDFs (where each page is an image) merge the same way as text-based PDFs. The tool combines all pages into one PDF without re-processing the images. The merged file will be larger if you add many heavy scanned documents, because the original image data is kept. For very large sets of scans, consider compressing the PDFs first with a separate tool if you need a smaller final size.
mergePdf.faq11Q: What happens if a PDF is corrupted or won't load?
mergePdf.faq11A: If one of your PDFs is damaged or in an unsupported format, the merge may fail or the tool may show an error. Remove the problematic file from the list and try again with the rest. If the PDF opens in another reader but not here, it may use features (e.g. certain encryption or attachments) that the in-browser library does not support. Saving a fresh copy from that reader as a standard PDF often fixes the issue.
mergePdf.faq12Q: Is the merged PDF searchable if the originals were searchable?
mergePdf.faq12A: Yes. When you merge PDFs that contain selectable text (searchable PDFs), the merged file keeps that text layer. You can still search and copy text in the result. If you merge PDFs that are scan-only (image-based) with no text layer, the merged PDF will also have no searchable text unless you run OCR separately. The tool does not add or remove text; it only combines the pages as they are.

compressPdf.label: Compress PDF
compressPdf.short: Reduce the size of PDF documents.
compressPdf.metaDescription: Reduce PDF file size online. Repackage your PDF in the browser. No account, in the browser.
compressPdf.editorialTitle: When and why to compress a PDF
compressPdf.editorialBody:
Compressing a PDF can reduce its file size so it is easier to email, upload, or store. This tool repackages your PDF in the browser using pdf-lib: it loads the document, copies all pages into a new PDF, and saves it. That can remove redundant data and sometimes reduce size without changing the content.

For larger size reductions, some tools re-encode images inside the PDF at lower quality. This tool keeps the existing content and repackages it, so quality is preserved. If your PDF is already well compressed, the result may be similar in size. Everything runs in your browser; your PDF never leaves your device.

Use this tool when you need a slightly smaller PDF for sharing or submission. For much smaller files you may need a desktop app that re-encodes images.
compressPdf.faq1Q: How do I compress a PDF online?
compressPdf.faq1A: Upload your PDF file. Click compress. The tool repackages the PDF in your browser using pdf-lib. Download the result. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
compressPdf.faq2Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
compressPdf.faq2A: No. Compression is done in your browser. Your PDF never leaves your device.
compressPdf.faq3Q: How much smaller will the file get?
compressPdf.faq3A: It depends on the original PDF. Repackaging can remove redundant data and sometimes reduce size. PDFs that are already well compressed may not shrink much.
compressPdf.faq4A: This tool repackages the PDF without re-encoding images or text. The content stays the same. Quality is preserved.
compressPdf.faq5Q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
compressPdf.faq5A: Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first. Open the PDF with the correct password in another app, save without password, then use that copy here.
compressPdf.faq6A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload your PDF, compress, and download. No app install required.
compressPdf.faq7A: This tool compresses one PDF at a time. For multiple files, use it repeatedly or merge them first and then compress the merged file.
compressPdf.faq8Q: What is the difference between compress and merge?
compressPdf.faq8A: Compress takes one PDF and tries to reduce its file size. Merge takes two or more PDFs and combines them into a single PDF. You can use both: merge first, then compress the result.
compressPdf.faq9Q: Why did my PDF get bigger?
compressPdf.faq9A: Sometimes repackaging can slightly increase size if the original was very tightly packed. If the tool re-embeds fonts or images differently, the result can be larger.
compressPdf.faq10Q: Is there a file size limit?
compressPdf.faq10A: There is no fixed limit. Very large PDFs may take longer and use more memory. For typical documents (e.g. under 100 MB), the tool works well.

jpgToPng.label: JPG → PNG
jpgToPng.metaDescription: Convert JPG to PNG online for free. No account, in the browser.
jpgToPng.editorialBody:
JPG is ideal for photos and small file sizes, but it does not support transparency and uses lossy compression. PNG supports transparency and is lossless, making it better for logos, graphics with sharp edges, and when you need to edit or overlay images without losing quality.

Converting JPG to PNG with this tool is useful when you need to add an image to a design that requires a transparent background, or when you want to avoid further quality loss from re-saving as JPG. The conversion runs entirely in your browser using the canvas API; your file never leaves your device.

Note: JPG does not store transparency. The output PNG will have an opaque background. For images that already have transparency, use a source format that supports it (e.g. PNG) before converting.
jpgToPng.faq1Q: How do I convert JPG to PNG online?
jpgToPng.faq1A: Upload your JPG file, then click convert. The tool uses the browser canvas to decode the JPG and encode a PNG. Download the result. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
jpgToPng.faq2A: PNG supports transparency and is lossless, so it is better for logos, graphics with sharp edges, or when you need to edit without losing quality. JPG is better for photos due to smaller file size.
jpgToPng.faq3A: Usually yes. PNG is lossless and often produces larger files than JPG for photos. For graphics with flat colors or transparency, PNG can be efficient.
jpgToPng.faq4Q: Are my images sent to a server?
jpgToPng.faq4A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using the canvas API. Your file never leaves your device.
jpgToPng.faq5A: JPG does not support transparency. When you convert JPG to PNG, the output has no transparency (opaque background). For transparent PNGs, start from an image that already has transparency.
jpgToPng.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in your mobile browser, upload a JPG, convert, and download the PNG. No app install required.
jpgToPng.faq7Q: Can I convert PNG to JPG?
jpgToPng.faq7A: This tool is for JPG to PNG only. Use a compress or convert image tool for PNG to JPG.
jpgToPng.faq8A: No. PNG is lossless. The pixel data is preserved. File size may be larger than the original JPG.
jpgToPng.faq9Q: What is the maximum image size?
jpgToPng.faq9A: Limits depend on your device and browser memory. Typical photos (several MB) work without issues.
jpgToPng.faq10A: This tool converts one file at a time. For batch conversion, use the tool repeatedly.

pngToJpg.label: PNG → JPG
pngToJpg.metaDescription: Convert PNG to JPG online for free. No account, in the browser.
pngToJpg.editorialBody:
PNG is lossless and supports transparency, but often produces larger files than JPG. Converting PNG to JPG reduces file size and is useful when you need a smaller image for web, email, or when the recipient expects JPG. Transparent areas in PNG become a solid background (usually white) in JPG.

This tool uses the browser canvas: it draws your PNG onto a white background (so transparency is replaced), then encodes the result as JPG. You can choose a quality level: lower values mean smaller files but more compression. Everything runs in your browser; your file never leaves your device.

If you need to keep transparency, stay with PNG or use another format that supports it. For photos or graphics where transparency is not needed, JPG is a good choice for smaller file size.
pngToJpg.faq1Q: How do I convert PNG to JPG online?
pngToJpg.faq1A: Upload your PNG file, choose a quality level if shown, then click convert. The tool uses the browser canvas to decode the PNG and encode a JPG. Download the result. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
pngToJpg.faq2A: JPG usually produces smaller file sizes than PNG and is widely supported. Converting PNG to JPG is useful when you need a smaller file for web, email, or when the recipient expects JPG. Note: JPG does not support transparency; transparent areas become a solid background.
pngToJpg.faq3A: Often yes, especially for photos or complex images. PNG is lossless and can be larger. JPG uses lossy compression, so the file is typically smaller. For simple graphics with flat colors, the difference may be small.
pngToJpg.faq4Q: Are my images sent to a server?
pngToJpg.faq4A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using the canvas API. Your file never leaves your device.
pngToJpg.faq5A: PNG can have transparency; JPG cannot. When you convert PNG to JPG, transparent areas are replaced with a solid background (usually white). If you need to keep transparency, stay with PNG.
pngToJpg.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in your mobile browser, upload a PNG, convert, and download the JPG. No app install required.
pngToJpg.faq7Q: Can I convert JPG to PNG?
pngToJpg.faq7A: This tool is for PNG to JPG only. Use the JPG to PNG tool for the reverse conversion.
pngToJpg.faq8A: Yes. JPG uses lossy compression, so some detail can be lost. For most photos the result is very good. You can often choose a quality level; higher quality means less loss but a larger file.
pngToJpg.faq9Q: What is the maximum image size?
pngToJpg.faq9A: Limits depend on your device and browser memory. Typical images (several MB) work without issues.
pngToJpg.faq10A: This tool converts one file at a time. For batch conversion, use the tool repeatedly.

imageToPdf.editorialBody:
Turning images into a single PDF makes them easier to share, submit, or archive as one document. Many forms and systems accept only PDF. Each image you upload becomes one page in the PDF, in the order you choose.

This tool uses pdf-lib in your browser to build the PDF. You can add multiple images (JPG or PNG), drag to reorder them, then create the PDF. No data is sent to any server; everything runs on your device.

The resulting PDF contains embedded images. Text in those images is not selectable or searchable. For searchable PDFs you would need an OCR tool or a service that adds text layers.
imageToPdf.faq1Q: How do I convert images to PDF online?
imageToPdf.faq1A: Upload one or more images (JPG or PNG). They appear in a list. Optionally reorder them, then click the button to create a PDF. Each image becomes one page. Download the PDF. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
imageToPdf.faq2Q: Are my images sent to a server?
imageToPdf.faq2A: No. The tool uses pdf-lib in your browser to build the PDF. Your images never leave your device.
imageToPdf.faq3A: JPG (JPEG) and PNG. Each image is embedded as one page in the PDF.
imageToPdf.faq4A: Yes. After uploading, you can drag the image rows to change the order. The PDF will be generated with pages in that order.
imageToPdf.faq5Q: What size will the PDF be?
imageToPdf.faq5A: The PDF size depends on the size and number of images. Each image is embedded in the PDF, so the file can be large if you use many high-resolution images.
imageToPdf.faq6A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload images from your gallery, optionally reorder, and download the PDF. No app install required.
imageToPdf.faq7Q: Can I add more images after uploading?
imageToPdf.faq7A: Yes. Use the add images button again to add more. They are appended to the list. You can clear the list and start over if needed.
imageToPdf.faq8A: No. The PDF contains images. Text in the images is not selectable or searchable. For searchable PDFs you would need OCR or a tool that adds text layers.
imageToPdf.faq9A: A single PDF is easier to share than many image files. PDFs are standard for documents, forms, and submissions. Converting images to PDF is useful for reports, portfolios, or when a system only accepts PDF.
imageToPdf.faq10A: There is no fixed limit. Very many or very large images may use a lot of memory and take longer. For typical use (e.g. under 50 images), the tool works well.

imageToWebp.label: Image → WebP
imageToWebp.short: Convert to WebP for smaller files.
imageToWebp.metaDescription: Convert images to WebP online. No account, in the browser.
imageToWebp.step3Description: Your image has been converted to WebP. Download it below.
imageToWebp.errorImageOnly: Please select a JPG, PNG or WebP image.
imageToWebp.editorialBody:
WebP often produces smaller file sizes than JPG or PNG at similar quality, which speeds up web pages and saves storage. All modern browsers support WebP. Converting to WebP is useful for websites, apps, and when you want to keep quality while reducing file size.

This tool uses the browser Canvas API: it loads your image, draws it on a canvas, and exports it as WebP with the quality level you choose. Lower quality values give smaller files; higher values keep more detail. Everything runs in your browser; your file never leaves your device.

Use WebP when your platform supports it (websites, modern apps). For maximum compatibility with older systems or email clients, JPG may be safer. Use the quality slider to balance size and quality.
imageToWebp.faq1Q: How do I convert an image to WebP online?
imageToWebp.faq1A: Upload your image (JPG, PNG or WebP). Set the quality with the slider (0–100; 80 is a good default). Click "Convert to WebP" and download the result. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
imageToWebp.faq2A: WebP often produces smaller file sizes than JPG or PNG at similar visual quality, which speeds up web pages. All modern browsers support WebP. Converting to WebP is useful for websites, apps, and when you want to save space without losing much quality.
imageToWebp.faq3Q: Are my images sent to a server?
imageToWebp.faq3A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using the Canvas API. Your file never leaves your device.
imageToWebp.faq4Q: What does the quality slider do?
imageToWebp.faq4A: Lower values (e.g. 60) give smaller files but more compression; higher values (e.g. 90) keep more detail but larger files. We recommend 75–85 for a good balance. You can compare file size after conversion.
imageToWebp.faq5A: You can upload JPG (JPEG), PNG, and WebP. The output is always WebP. If you already have WebP, you can re-encode it at a different quality.
imageToWebp.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in your mobile browser, upload an image, set quality, convert, and download. No app install required.
imageToWebp.faq7A: WebP supports transparency. If your source is PNG or WebP with transparency, the output WebP can keep it. JPG has no transparency, so the result will be opaque.
imageToWebp.faq8A: This tool converts one file at a time. For batch conversion, use the tool repeatedly or combine with other image tools.
imageToWebp.faq9Q: What is the maximum image size?
imageToWebp.faq9A: Limits depend on your device and browser memory. Typical photos (several MB) work without issues. Very large images may take longer.
imageToWebp.faq10A: WebP often gives 25–35% smaller files than JPG at similar quality. Use WebP when your platform supports it (websites, modern apps). Use JPG when you need maximum compatibility (e.g. some email clients or older systems).

webpToJpg.label: WebP → JPG
webpToJpg.metaDescription: Convert WebP to JPG online for free. No account, in the browser.
webpToJpg.editorialBody:
WebP offers good compression and quality but is not supported everywhere. JPG is universally supported and expected by many apps, forms, and printers. Converting WebP to JPG makes your image compatible with any device or service that only accepts JPG.

This tool uses the browser canvas: it draws your WebP onto a white background (so transparency is replaced if present), then encodes the result as JPG. You can choose a quality level: lower values mean smaller files but more compression. Everything runs in your browser; your file never leaves your device.

If you need to keep transparency or the smallest file size, stay with WebP or use PNG. For maximum compatibility and sharing, JPG is the safe choice.
webpToJpg.faq1Q: How do I convert WebP to JPG online?
webpToJpg.faq1A: Upload your WebP file, choose a quality level if shown, then click convert. The tool uses the browser canvas to decode the WebP and encode a JPG. Download the result. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
webpToJpg.faq2A: WebP is efficient but not all apps or websites support it. JPG is universally supported. Converting to JPG is useful for sharing, printing, or when the recipient or system expects JPG.
webpToJpg.faq3A: Often JPG is larger than WebP at similar quality, but it depends on the image. You can choose a quality level: lower values mean smaller files but more compression.
webpToJpg.faq4Q: Are my images sent to a server?
webpToJpg.faq4A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using the canvas API. Your file never leaves your device.
webpToJpg.faq5A: WebP can have transparency; JPG cannot. When you convert WebP to JPG, transparent areas are replaced with a solid background (usually white). If you need transparency, keep the WebP or use PNG.
webpToJpg.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in your mobile browser, upload a WebP, convert, and download the JPG. No app install required.
webpToJpg.faq7Q: Can I convert JPG to WebP?

webpToJpg.faq10Q: Can I convert multiple WebP files?

splitPdf.label: Split PDF
splitPdf.short: Split a PDF into one file per page, download as ZIP.
splitPdf.metaDescription: Split a PDF so each page becomes a separate PDF. Download all pages as a ZIP. No account, in the browser.
splitPdf.step3Description: Your PDF has been split. Download the ZIP containing one PDF per page.
splitPdf.editorialTitle: When and why to split a PDF
splitPdf.editorialBody:
Splitting a PDF turns each page into its own file. That is useful when you need to send only certain pages, reuse single pages in other documents, or when a system accepts only one-page PDFs. This tool splits in the browser: every page becomes a separate PDF, and all are packed into a single ZIP for download.

The tool uses pdf-lib to load your PDF and copy each page into a new document. No data is sent to any server; everything runs on your device. After splitting, you get a ZIP file containing page-1.pdf, page-2.pdf, and so on. You can extract the ZIP and use or send only the pages you need.

For the opposite operation—combining several PDFs into one—use the Merge PDF tool. Split and merge are complementary: split to get single pages, merge to put documents together.
splitPdf.faq1Q: How do I split a PDF online?
splitPdf.faq1A: Upload your PDF file. The tool loads it in your browser and splits it so each page becomes a separate PDF. Click the button to split, then download all pages as a single ZIP file. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
splitPdf.faq2Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
splitPdf.faq2A: No. Splitting is done in your browser using pdf-lib. Your PDF never leaves your device.
splitPdf.faq3Q: Can I choose which pages to split?
splitPdf.faq3A: This tool splits every page into its own PDF. You get one PDF per page, all bundled in a ZIP. If you need only certain pages, extract them from the ZIP after download.
splitPdf.faq4Q: What are the output file names?
splitPdf.faq4A: Each page is saved as a separate PDF in the ZIP, named by page number (e.g. page-1.pdf, page-2.pdf). You can rename them after extracting the ZIP.
splitPdf.faq5Q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
splitPdf.faq5A: Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first. Open the PDF with the correct password in another app, save without password, then use that copy here.
splitPdf.faq6A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload your PDF, split, and download the ZIP. No app install required.
splitPdf.faq7A: There is no fixed limit. Very long PDFs may take longer and use more memory. For typical documents (e.g. under 100 pages), splitting works well.
splitPdf.faq8Q: What is the difference between split and merge?
splitPdf.faq8A: Split takes one PDF and creates separate PDFs (one per page), then packs them in a ZIP. Merge takes two or more PDFs and combines them into a single PDF. They are opposite operations.
splitPdf.faq9Q: Can I split only a range of pages?
splitPdf.faq9A: This tool splits all pages. Each page becomes one PDF in the ZIP. If you need only pages 3–5, download the ZIP and keep only those files after extracting.
splitPdf.faq10A: No. The tool copies each page as-is into a new PDF. Content and quality are preserved. No re-encoding or compression is applied.

pngToPdf.label: PNG → PDF
pngToPdf.short: Convert a single PNG to a one-page PDF.
pngToPdf.metaDescription: Convert one PNG image to a single-page PDF. No account, in the browser.

pngToPdf.editorialTitle: Why convert a PNG to PDF
pngToPdf.editorialBody:
Converting a single PNG to a one-page PDF is useful when a form, system, or recipient expects a PDF rather than an image. Many workflows accept only PDF. This tool embeds your PNG in a new PDF with one page, so you get a standard document that opens in any PDF reader.

The tool uses pdf-lib in your browser to create the PDF. Your PNG is embedded as-is; no re-encoding or resizing is done. Everything runs on your device; no data is sent to any server. The result is a one-page PDF whose dimensions match your image.

For multiple images in one PDF, use the Images to PDF tool instead. For a single image that must be submitted as PDF, this tool is the simplest option.
pngToPdf.faq1Q: How do I convert a PNG to PDF online?
pngToPdf.faq1A: Upload your PNG file. The tool embeds it in a single-page PDF in your browser using pdf-lib. Click the button to create the PDF, then download. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
pngToPdf.faq2Q: Are my images sent to a server?
pngToPdf.faq2A: No. The tool uses pdf-lib in your browser to build the PDF. Your PNG never leaves your device.
pngToPdf.faq3A: A single PDF is easier to share or submit than an image file in many cases. Many forms and systems accept only PDF. Converting one PNG to a one-page PDF is useful for documents, forms, or when the recipient expects PDF.
pngToPdf.faq4A: PNG can have transparency. When embedded in a PDF, transparent areas may appear as white or as defined in the PDF. The tool embeds the PNG as-is; complex transparency is preserved where the PDF format allows.
pngToPdf.faq5A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload your PNG, create the PDF, and download. No app install required.
pngToPdf.faq6Q: Can I add multiple PNGs to one PDF?
pngToPdf.faq6A: This tool creates a one-page PDF from one PNG. For multiple images in one PDF, use the Images to PDF tool instead.
pngToPdf.faq7A: No. The PDF contains your image as a single page. Text in the image is not selectable or searchable. For searchable PDFs you would need OCR or a tool that adds text layers.
pngToPdf.faq8Q: What size will the PDF be?
pngToPdf.faq8A: The PDF size depends on the PNG. The image is embedded in the PDF, so the file is typically similar in size to or slightly larger than the original PNG.
pngToPdf.faq9Q: Can I convert JPG to PDF?
pngToPdf.faq9A: This tool is for PNG to PDF only. For JPG or multiple images, use the Images to PDF tool.
pngToPdf.faq10Q: Is there a file size limit?
pngToPdf.faq10A: There is no fixed limit. Very large PNGs may take longer and use more memory. For typical images (e.g. under 20 MB), the tool works well.

svgToPng.label: SVG → PNG
svgToPng.short: Convert SVG to PNG in the browser.
svgToPng.metaDescription: Convert SVG to PNG online for free. No account, in the browser.
svgToPng.step3Description: Your PNG has been created. Download it below.
svgToPng.editorialBody:
SVG is a vector format that scales well but is not supported everywhere—some social media, forms, or apps only accept raster images like PNG. Converting SVG to PNG gives you a fixed-size image that works in any context.

This tool loads your SVG in the browser, draws it onto a canvas at the SVG's natural dimensions (or a fallback size), and exports the canvas as PNG. No data is sent to any server; everything runs on your device. Transparency is preserved where the format allows.

For the opposite conversion (PNG to vector), you would need a tracing tool. For resizing or compressing PNGs, use the resize or compress image tools.
svgToPng.faq1Q: How do I convert SVG to PNG online?
svgToPng.faq1A: Upload your SVG file. The tool loads it as an image in your browser, draws it onto a canvas, then exports the canvas as PNG. Click convert and download. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
svgToPng.faq2Q: Are my files sent to a server?

svgToPng.faq5A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload your SVG, convert, and download the PNG. No app install required.

rotatePdf.label: Rotate PDF
rotatePdf.metaDescription: Rotate all pages of a PDF by 90°, 180°, or 270°. No account, in the browser.
rotatePdf.step3Description: Your PDF has been rotated. Download it below.
rotatePdf.editorialTitle: When and why to rotate a PDF
rotatePdf.editorialBody:
Sometimes a PDF is scanned or exported with pages in the wrong orientation. Rotating the PDF corrects the layout so that readers see the content right-side up. This tool applies the same rotation (90°, 180°, or 270°) to every page of your PDF.

The tool uses pdf-lib in your browser to load the PDF and set the rotation metadata on each page. No re-encoding or re-compression is applied; content and quality are preserved. Your file never leaves your device; no data is sent to any server.

If you need to rotate only some pages, or combine rotation with other edits, use a PDF editor. For merging or splitting PDFs, use the Merge PDF or Split PDF tools.
rotatePdf.faq1Q: How do I rotate a PDF online?
rotatePdf.faq1A: Upload your PDF file. Choose a rotation angle (90°, 180°, or 270°) using the buttons. Click the rotate button. The tool applies the rotation to every page in your browser using pdf-lib, then you download the result. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
rotatePdf.faq2Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
rotatePdf.faq2A: No. Rotation is done in your browser using pdf-lib. Your PDF never leaves your device.
rotatePdf.faq3Q: Can I rotate only some pages?
rotatePdf.faq3A: This tool rotates all pages by the same angle. If you need to rotate only certain pages, use a PDF editor that supports per-page rotation.
rotatePdf.faq4A: You can rotate by 90° (clockwise), 180°, or 270° (equivalent to 90° counter-clockwise). These cover the typical needs for correcting orientation.
rotatePdf.faq5Q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?

rotatePdf.faq6A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload your PDF, choose the angle, rotate, and download. No app install required.
rotatePdf.faq7A: No. The tool sets the page rotation metadata in the PDF. Content and quality are preserved; no re-encoding or re-compression is applied.
rotatePdf.faq8Q: Why is my PDF rotated the wrong way?
rotatePdf.faq8A: If the result is not what you expected, try the other angle (e.g. 270° instead of 90°). Rotation is applied clockwise: 90° turns the page once to the right.
rotatePdf.faq9A: There is no fixed limit. Very long PDFs may take longer and use more memory. For typical documents (e.g. under 100 pages), rotation works well.
rotatePdf.faq10Q: Can I rotate and merge in one go?
rotatePdf.faq10A: This tool only rotates. To rotate and then combine with other PDFs, rotate first, download, then use the Merge PDF tool with the rotated file and others.

gifToMp4.label: GIF → MP4
gifToMp4.short: Convert GIF to MP4 for smaller file size.
gifToMp4.metaDescription: Convert GIF to MP4 online. Smaller files, same quality. No account, in the browser with FFmpeg.wasm.
gifToMp4.loadingFfmpeg: Loading FFmpeg... (this may take a few seconds)
gifToMp4.step3Description: Your GIF has been converted to MP4. Download it below.
gifToMp4.errorLoadFfmpeg: Failed to load FFmpeg. Check your connection and try again.
gifToMp4.editorialBody:
GIFs are large for the quality they deliver. Converting to MP4 (H.264) produces much smaller files with similar or better visual quality, and MP4 is supported everywhere. Many platforms (Twitter, Discord, websites) prefer video (MP4) over GIF for inline playback.

This tool uses FFmpeg.wasm: FFmpeg runs in your browser via WebAssembly, so your GIF is never uploaded to a server. The first time you use the tool, FFmpeg may take a few seconds to load. A progress bar shows conversion status. The output uses settings (yuv420p, faststart) that keep compatibility and good quality.

Use GIF to MP4 when you want to reduce file size or when the target platform expects video. For creating a GIF from a video, you would need a different tool.
gifToMp4.faq1Q: How do I convert a GIF to MP4 online?
gifToMp4.faq1A: Upload your GIF file. The tool uses FFmpeg.wasm in your browser to convert it to MP4. Click "Convert to MP4"; a progress bar shows while processing. When done, download the MP4. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
gifToMp4.faq2A: MP4 (H.264) is much smaller than GIF for the same visual quality and is supported everywhere. Converting GIF to MP4 reduces file size and improves playback on websites and social media. Many platforms prefer video (MP4) over GIF.
gifToMp4.faq3Q: Are my files sent to a server?
gifToMp4.faq3A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser using FFmpeg.wasm. Your GIF never leaves your device.
gifToMp4.faq4Q: Why does FFmpeg take a few seconds to load?
gifToMp4.faq4A: FFmpeg.wasm is a large WebAssembly module. It is downloaded once (from a CDN) and then cached by the browser. The first time you use the tool or after clearing cache, you will see a loading state for a few seconds.
gifToMp4.faq5A: Yes, in browsers that support WebAssembly and the required APIs. Some older mobile browsers may be slower or have limits. Try it in the latest Chrome or Safari.
gifToMp4.faq6A: The tool uses settings that keep good visual quality while ensuring compatibility (e.g. yuv420p, faststart). The MP4 is typically much smaller than the original GIF with similar or better appearance.
gifToMp4.faq7Q: Can I convert MP4 to GIF?
gifToMp4.faq7A: This tool is for GIF to MP4 only. For video to GIF you would need a different tool that creates animated GIFs from video.
gifToMp4.faq8Q: Is there a file size limit?
gifToMp4.faq8A: Practical limits depend on your device memory. Very large GIFs may take longer or cause the browser to slow down. Typical GIFs (a few MB) work without issues.
gifToMp4.faq9Q: Why use MP4 instead of GIF on a website?
gifToMp4.faq9A: MP4 loads faster, uses less bandwidth, and often looks better than GIF. Modern HTML5 video supports MP4; you can autoplay, mute, and loop it like a GIF. Many sites (e.g. Twitter, Discord) show MP4s as inline video.
gifToMp4.faq10Q: Does it work in all browsers?
gifToMp4.faq10A: FFmpeg.wasm requires a modern browser with WebAssembly support. Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge (recent versions) work. Some corporate or very old browsers may not support it.

extractPdfPages.editorialBody:
Sometimes you need only part of a PDF—a few pages for a report, or specific sections to share. Extracting pages creates a new PDF containing only the pages you choose, so you do not have to send the whole file or manually delete pages elsewhere.

This tool uses pdf-lib in your browser: you upload the PDF, enter a page range (e.g. 1-3, 5, 7-9), and the tool copies those pages into a new document. The range is validated so you cannot request pages that do not exist. Everything runs client-side; your PDF never leaves your device.

Use extract when you need a subset of pages in one new PDF. Use Split PDF when you want every page as a separate file.
extractPdfPages.faq1Q: How do I extract pages from a PDF online?
extractPdfPages.faq1A: Upload your PDF file. The tool shows the total number of pages. Enter the page range you want (e.g. 1-3, 5, 7-9) in the text field. Click "Extract pages" to create a new PDF containing only those pages, then download. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.
extractPdfPages.faq2Q: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
extractPdfPages.faq2A: No. Extraction is done in your browser using pdf-lib. Your PDF never leaves your device.
extractPdfPages.faq3Q: What format is the page range?
extractPdfPages.faq3A: You can enter single pages (e.g. 5), ranges (e.g. 1-3 for pages 1, 2, 3), or a combination separated by commas (e.g. 1-3, 5, 7-9). Pages are 1-based (first page is 1).
extractPdfPages.faq4Q: What if I enter an invalid range?
extractPdfPages.faq4A: The tool validates the input. If a page number is out of bounds (e.g. page 20 when the PDF has 10 pages) or the format is invalid, an error message is shown. Correct the range and try again.
extractPdfPages.faq5Q: Does it work with password-protected PDFs?
extractPdfPages.faq5A: Password-protected PDFs must be unlocked first. Open the PDF with the correct password in another app, save without password, then use that copy here.
extractPdfPages.faq6A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload your PDF, enter the page range, extract, and download. No app install required.
extractPdfPages.faq7Q: Is the order of pages preserved?
extractPdfPages.faq7A: Yes. The extracted PDF contains the selected pages in the order you specified (e.g. 1-3, 5, 7-9 gives pages 1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 8, 9 in that order).
extractPdfPages.faq8A: Yes. Enter a range that covers all pages (e.g. 1-10 for a 10-page PDF). The result is a copy of the original. For splitting each page into a separate file, use the Split PDF tool.
extractPdfPages.faq9A: There is no fixed limit. Very long PDFs may take longer and use more memory. For typical documents (e.g. under 100 pages), extraction works well.
extractPdfPages.faq10Q: What is the difference between extract and split?
extractPdfPages.faq10A: Extract creates one PDF containing only the pages you choose (e.g. pages 2, 5, 7). Split creates one PDF per page and packs them in a ZIP. Use extract when you want a single PDF with selected pages; use split when you want every page as a separate file.

resizeImage.short: Fit photos to websites, CVs and forms.
resizeImage.metaDescription: Resize images by width and height. No account, in the browser.
resizeImage.editorialTitle: When and why to resize images
resizeImage.editorialBody:
Resizing an image changes its pixel dimensions so it fits a specific size requirement—for example a website banner, a CV photo, or a form that limits file dimensions. Reducing dimensions also reduces file size, which can help when uploading or sending images by email.

This tool uses the browser canvas API: you set the desired width and height (or one dimension with aspect ratio locked), and the image is redrawn at the new size. You can resize to make an image smaller or larger; for best quality, avoid enlarging small images too much, as that can look soft or pixelated.

All processing happens in your browser. Your image is never uploaded to any server, so you keep full control and privacy.

resizeImage.errorInvalidDimensions: Enter valid width and height (numbers greater than 0).
resizeImage.faq1Q: How do I resize an image online?
resizeImage.faq1A: Upload your image (JPG, PNG, WebP), enter the desired width or height (or both), then click resize. The tool uses the browser canvas to resize. Download the result. Everything runs locally; no data is sent to any server.
resizeImage.faq2A: Resizing to a smaller size reduces pixel count, so fine detail can be lost. Resizing to a larger size stretches pixels and can look soft. For best results, resize down when you need a smaller image; avoid enlarging small images too much.
resizeImage.faq3A: Yes. If you only enter width or only height, the other dimension is calculated automatically to preserve the original aspect ratio. You can also enter both to force specific dimensions (image may be stretched).
resizeImage.faq4A: You can upload JPG, PNG, and WebP. The output format matches the input. These are the most common image formats for web and photos.
resizeImage.faq5Q: Are my images uploaded to a server?
resizeImage.faq5A: No. All processing happens in your browser using the canvas API. Your image never leaves your device.
resizeImage.faq6Q: Is there a file size limit?
resizeImage.faq6A: There is no fixed limit. Very large images may take longer or use more memory. Typical photos (a few MB) work without issues.
resizeImage.faq7Q: Why would I resize an image?
resizeImage.faq7A: Common reasons: fit a photo to a website or form size limit, create thumbnails, reduce dimensions for email, or match requirements for CVs, social media, or print.
resizeImage.faq8A: Yes. The tool runs in the mobile browser. Upload from your gallery, set dimensions, and download. No app install required.
resizeImage.faq9A: This tool processes one image at a time. For multiple images, use it repeatedly or combine with other tools.
resizeImage.faq10Q: What is the maximum output size?
resizeImage.faq10A: Practical limits depend on your device and browser. Canvas has limits (often 16384px per side). For typical use (e.g. under 4000px), there are no issues.

Converting a PDF to JPG turns each page into an image file that you can use in presentations, websites, or anywhere that expects a photo or graphic. JPGs are widely supported and easy to insert in documents, emails, or social media.

This tool uses PDF.js in your browser to render each page onto a canvas and then encode it as a JPG. You can download each page as a separate file or all pages in one ZIP. Processing is entirely client-side: your PDF never leaves your device.

The output is an image, so text in the JPG is no longer selectable or searchable. For editable text, use a PDF-to-text tool instead.

pdfToJpg.faq9A: Each page is converted to a separate JPG. You get multiple files or one ZIP containing all pages in order.
pdfToJpg.faq10A: There is no fixed limit. Very long PDFs may take longer and use more memory. For typical documents (e.g. under 50 pages), conversion works well.

This tool uses the same client-side approach as PDF to JPG: your file never leaves your device. You can download each page as a separate PNG or all pages in one ZIP. For smaller file sizes without transparency, use PDF to JPG instead.

Use PDF to PNG when you need lossless quality or transparency; use PDF to JPG when you want smaller files for web or email.

pdfToPng.faq1A: Upload your PDF file. The tool renders each page to an image in the browser using PDF.js and the canvas, then encodes each as PNG. You can download each page as a separate PNG or all as a ZIP. Everything runs in your browser; no data is sent to any server.

pdfToPng.faq4A: PNG is lossless and supports transparency. Use PDF to PNG when you need exact pixel reproduction, transparency, or when you will edit the images. Use PDF to JPG when you want smaller files and do not need transparency.

heicToJpg.short: Convert iPhone HEIC photos to JPG.
heicToJpg.metaDescription: Convert HEIC (iPhone) photos to JPG online. One or multiple files, preview, download single or ZIP. In the browser.
heicToJpg.editorialBody: HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones and saves space, but many websites, apps, and email recipients expect JPG. Converting to JPG makes your photos easy to share and open anywhere. This tool runs in your browser, so your photos never leave your device.
heicToJpg.faq1A: HEIC is the default photo format on iPhones. Converting to JPG makes photos easier to share. Conversion runs in your browser; files never leave your device.
heicToJpg.faq2A: Yes. Select multiple HEIC files. The tool shows progress and lets you download each JPG or all in a ZIP.

heicToJpg.faq4Q: Are my photos sent to a server?
heicToJpg.faq4A: No. Conversion runs entirely in your browser. Your files never leave your device.
heicToJpg.faq5A: When you convert many files, one ZIP is faster than saving each JPG individually.
heicToJpg.faq6Q: Does it work on iPhone and iPad?
heicToJpg.faq6A: Yes. Open the tool in Safari (or another browser) on your iPhone or iPad, then tap to add HEIC photos from your camera roll or Files app. The conversion runs in the browser and you can download each JPG or a ZIP. No app install is required.
heicToJpg.faq7A: Basic metadata such as date taken can be preserved when the conversion is done in the browser, depending on the library used. For full EXIF (camera model, GPS, etc.) preservation, some tools may strip or simplify it when encoding JPG. If you need exact EXIF, check the output or use a dedicated desktop tool.
heicToJpg.faq8A: The converted JPG keeps the same dimensions (pixel width and height) as the original HEIC. Only the format and compression change; resolution is not reduced. You get a standard JPG that you can use for print or web at the same size as the source.
heicToJpg.faq9Q: Can I convert HEIC to PNG or WebP instead?
heicToJpg.faq9A: This tool converts HEIC to JPG only. JPG is the most widely supported format for sharing and is sufficient for most uses. If you need PNG (e.g. for transparency) or WebP, you would need to convert HEIC to JPG first, then use another tool to convert JPG to the desired format, or use a converter that supports HEIC to PNG/WebP directly.
heicToJpg.faq10Q: How do I open a HEIC file on Windows/PC?
heicToJpg.faq10A: Windows does not open HEIC files natively; you may see a message that an app is needed. Converting HEIC to JPG with this tool solves the problem: upload the HEIC here, download the JPG, and open it in any Windows app. No extra software is required on your PC.
heicToJpg.faq11Q: What is the difference between HEIC and JPG?
heicToJpg.faq11A: HEIC typically produces smaller file sizes than JPG at similar visual quality, which is why iPhones use it. JPG is much more widely supported: it opens everywhere (Windows, websites, email, social media), while HEIC often requires conversion or specific apps. JPG uses lossy compression, so converting from HEIC to JPG can slightly reduce quality, but for most uses the result is excellent. In short: HEIC means smaller files and better compatibility with Apple devices; JPG means universal compatibility and slightly larger files.
heicToJpg.faq12Q: Can I convert a JPG back to HEIC?
heicToJpg.faq12A: Converting JPG back to HEIC is possible with some tools but usually not useful: JPG is lossy, so you would be saving already compressed data into HEIC without regaining the original quality or file size. For iPhone users, the best approach is to keep HEIC originals on the device or in iCloud and convert to JPG only when you need to share or use the photo elsewhere. This tool is for HEIC to JPG only; to keep new iPhone photos in HEIC, leave the camera format set to HEIC in Settings.
